exposure: PBM effects of semiconductor lasers at 658 and 660 nm with 100, 150 and 350 mW output powers

laser therapy using indium gallium aluminum phosphide (InGaAlP) semiconductor linear scanning type with beam cross section of 12 cm(2) and the output power of 100 mW at 658 nm exposing a therapeutic dose of 2 J/cm(2)
Photobiomodulation using semiconductor lasers at 658 and 660 nm with 100, 150 and 350 mW output powers
cohort: 40 women undergoing their first cesarean section
finding: Photobiomodulation therapy using semiconductor lasers resulted in significantly better wound healing scores compared to conventional wound care methods in women after cesarean section.
